title: Pressure-tuning of electronic structure of CeTe3 probed by femtosecond collective mode spectroscopy
authors: Chandra V. Kotyada, Priyanka Yogi, Amon P. Lanz, Rolf Heid, Jonas Tauch, Manuel Obergfell, Hanjo Schaefer, Paula Giraldo-Gallo, Ian R. Fisher, Alexej Pashkin, Jure Demsar
abstract: We use femtosecond optical spectroscopy to study the evolution of coherent order-parameter dynamics in the prototypical charge-density-wave (CDW) system CeTe3 under hydrostatic pressure. The CDW transition temperature decreases from approximately 570 K at ambient pressure to near room temperature at approximately 6 GPa. The pressure dependence of the order-parameter recovery dynamics indicates enhanced electron-phonon coupling with increasing pressure, implying that CDW suppression is driven predominantly by the reduction in Fermi-surface nesting. Above 7 GPa, no evidence of CDW order is observed down to cryogenic temperatures. Concurrently, the relaxation dynamics exhibit significant slowing down at low-temperatures, consistent with emerging heavy-electron behaviour due to pressure-enhanced hybridization between localized Ce 4f levels and itinerant carriers.
summary: This experimental work uses femtosecond spectroscopy to track how hydrostatic pressure suppresses the Charge-Density-Wave (CDW) state in CeTe3. The results show that CDW suppression is linked to changes in Fermi-surface nesting, while high pressures induce heavy-electron behavior via enhanced hybridization between localized Ce 4f electrons and itinerant carriers.
main_problem: The study investigates how hydrostatic pressure tunes the coherent order-parameter dynamics of a Charge-Density-Wave (CDW) state in the material CeTe3.
main_result: CDW suppression occurs as pressure increases, driven by reduced Fermi-surface nesting, and at high pressures, the system exhibits signatures of heavy-electron behavior due to enhanced Ce 4f hybridization.
method: The research employs femtosecond optical spectroscopy (pump-probe) to probe the out-of-equilibrium dynamics of the electronic order parameter as a function of temperature and pressure.
model_or_system: The system is CeTe3, a rare-earth tritelluride known for its incommensurate CDW. The analysis focuses on the evolution of the CDW order parameter dynamics, which couples electronic and lattice degrees of freedom.
key_observables: Real-time dynamics of the order parameter, amplitude modes (AMs), relaxation time ($\tau_0$), and the CDW transition temperature ($T_{\text{CDW}}$).
important_parameters: Hydrostatic pressure (up to 7.4 GPa), Temperature (down to cryogenic levels), and the lattice constant.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on fitting the time-domain signal using a specific functional form that separates overdamped and oscillatory components.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the pressure dependence of $T_{\text{CDW}}$ (decreasing from 570 K to room temperature at $\sim 6$ GPa), the softening and damping of oscillatory modes near $T_{\text{CDW}}$, and the anomalous slowing down of relaxation dynamics at high pressure.
paper_structure: The paper systematically maps the phase diagram by measuring the CDW dynamics across varying pressures and temperatures, first establishing the CDW suppression mechanism, and then analyzing the resulting heavy-fermion-like behavior at high pressure.
why_interesting: The study uses ultrafast spectroscopy to track the collapse of an electronic order parameter (CDW) and the emergence of heavy-fermion physics, providing a dynamic view of competing ground states relevant to strongly correlated electron systems.
